concepts.title: Verb + a / di + infinitive
concepts.rule: Before an infinitive, many verbs need a (riuscire, continuare, cominciare, abituarsi, imparare, convincere/aiutare qualcuno a) or di (cercare, smettere, finire, decidere, sperare, ricordarsi, dimenticare, chiedere/dire a qualcuno di). Modals, sapere, preferire, desiderare and impersonal expressions take no preposition. Some verbs change meaning: finire di (stop) vs finire per (end up).
assessment: Uses a after verbs of beginning, continuing, managing and persuading (riuscire a, continuare a, convincere qualcuno a)
Uses di after verbs of trying, stopping, deciding, hoping and remembering (cercare di, smettere di, decidere di)
Uses no preposition after modals, sapere, preferire and desiderare
Distinguishes finire di / finire per and decidere di / decidersi a

lesson.intro: English uses 'to' before almost every infinitive ('I managed to', 'I tried to', 'I decided to'). Italian splits these verbs into an *a* group, a *di* group and a no-preposition group, and there's no reliable logic: you learn each verb with its preposition. Getting them right is a big step towards accurate C1 Italian.

rules.title: Verbs + a
rules.text: Mostly verbs of **beginning, continuing, managing, learning and moving towards** an action: *cominciare / iniziare a, continuare a, riuscire a, imparare a, abituarsi a, mettersi a, provare a, prepararsi a, andare / venire a*. Before a vowel *a* often becomes *ad*: *Sono riuscito **ad** aprire*.

examples.en: I can't (manage to) sleep.
It keeps raining.
I've got used to getting up early.

rules.title: Verbs + di
rules.text: Mostly verbs of **trying, stopping, deciding, thinking, hoping, remembering and fearing**: *cercare di, smettere di, finire di, decidere di, sperare di, pensare di, credere di, ricordarsi di, dimenticare / dimenticarsi di, temere di, accettare di, rifiutare di, sognare di*.

examples.en: I've stopped smoking.
Try to understand!
I hope to see you again soon.

rules.title: No preposition
rules.text: Modals (*potere, dovere, volere*), *sapere* (= know how to), *preferire, desiderare, osare*, causative *fare / lasciare*, and impersonal expressions (*bisogna, è meglio, è importante, mi piace*) take the bare infinitive.

examples.en: I prefer to stay at home.
Can you swim?
I like cooking.

rules.title: Verb + person + preposition
rules.text: Verbs with a person as object have their own pattern: *convincere / aiutare / invitare / costringere **qualcuno a***; *chiedere / dire / ordinare / permettere / impedire **a qualcuno di***.

head: Pattern
Verbs
Example
rows: convincere, aiutare, invitare, costringere, insegnare (a qualcuno a)
chiedere, dire, ordinare, permettere, impedire, consigliare

rules.title: Same verb, different meaning
rules.text: Some verbs change meaning with the preposition.

head: Verb
Meaning
Example
rows: to make up one's mind to

mistakes.why: *Sapere* = know how to: no preposition. (*So di avere ragione* = I know I'm right.)

tips: Rough rule: verbs of starting, continuing and moving forward like *a*; verbs of stopping, trying and mental states like *di*. Exceptions exist, so learn verbs in pairs: *provare a / cercare di*.
Put new verbs in your Error Bank as chunks: *riuscire a*, *smettere di*, not just the verb.
Use *ad* before *a-* (*ad aprire*). Before other vowels it's optional.

exercises.prompt: Con questo caldo non riesco ___ dormire.
exercises.en: With this heat I can't sleep.

exercises.prompt: Ho smesso ___ fumare due anni fa.
exercises.en: I stopped smoking two years ago.

exercises.prompt: Abbiamo deciso ___ cambiare casa.

traps.why: *Decidere* takes *di*. (*Decidersi a* = make up one's mind.)

exercises.en: We've decided to move house.

exercises.prompt: Stasera preferisco ___ restare a casa.
exercises.en: Tonight I'd rather stay home.

exercises.prompt: Mi ha convinto ___ partire con lui.
exercises.en: He persuaded me to leave with him.

exercises.prompt: Continua ___ piovere da stamattina.
exercises.en: It's been raining non-stop since this morning.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct preposition. (Meaning: they ended up getting divorced.)
exercises.prompt: Dopo anni di litigi, hanno finito ___ divorziare.

traps.why: *Finire di* = stop doing. 'End up doing' is *finire **per***.

exercises.en: After years of arguing, they ended up getting divorced.

exercises.prompt: Sai ___ guidare la moto?

optionWhy.2: *Sapere di* + infinitive means 'know that…' about oneself (*So di sbagliare*). 'Can you ride?' = *Sai guidare?*

exercises.explanation: *Sapere* = know how to → bare infinitive: **Sai guidare?**
exercises.en: Can you ride a motorbike?

exercises.prompt: Non mi sono ancora abituato ___ alzarmi alle sei.
exercises.en: I still haven't got used to getting up at six.

exercises.prompt: Le ho chiesto ___ aspettarmi davanti al cinema.
exercises.en: I asked her to wait for me outside the cinema.

exercises.prompt: Ho provato a chiamarti tutto il giorno.
answers: Ho cercato di chiamarti tutto il giorno
exercises.en: I tried to call you all day.

exercises.prompt: I forgot to buy the bread.
answers: (Mi sono dimenticato|Mi sono dimenticata|Ho dimenticato) di comprare il pane

traps.match: (Mi sono dimenticato|Mi sono dimenticata|Ho dimenticato) comprare il pane

exercises.en: I forgot to buy the bread.

exercises.prompt: My father taught me to swim.
answers: Mio padre mi ha insegnato a nuotare

traps.why: No article with singular family members after a possessive: *mio padre*.

traps.match: Mio padre mi ha insegnato nuotare

exercises.en: My father taught me to swim.

exercises.prompt: I hope to see you again soon.
I'm thinking of going to Sicily this summer.
answers: (Penso|Sto pensando) di andare in Sicilia (quest'estate|questa estate)
(Quest'estate|Questa estate) (penso|sto pensando) di andare in Sicilia
exercises.en: I'm thinking of going to Sicily this summer.

exercises.prompt: Tell a friend you've finally managed to find a flat.
answers: Finalmente sono (riuscito|riuscita) a trovare (un appartamento|una casa|casa)
Sono finalmente (riuscito|riuscita) a trovare (un appartamento|una casa|casa)
Sono (riuscito|riuscita) finalmente a trovare (un appartamento|una casa|casa)
exercises.en: I've finally managed to find a flat.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct preposition. (Meaning: he finally made up his mind.)
exercises.prompt: Dopo settimane di dubbi, finalmente si è deciso ___ parlarle.

optionWhy.1: *Decidere di* (no *si*). The reflexive *decidersi* (make up one's mind) takes *a*.

exercises.explanation: *Decidersi* **a** = finally make up one's mind to.
exercises.en: After weeks of doubt, he finally made up his mind to talk to her.

concepts.title: Prepositions of place and time: nuances
concepts.rule: A with cities and small islands, in with countries, regions and large islands (articulated if plural or qualified: negli Stati Uniti); in via / in piazza; da + person (dal medico, da Marco). Fra/tra + time = in (future). Da + present tense for actions still going on (Studio l'italiano da tre anni); per for a finished or limited duration; in for time taken.
assessment: Chooses a for cities and in for countries, regions and big islands, with articulated forms where needed
Uses da for going to / being at someone's place or a professional's
Uses da + present for ongoing durations and per for completed ones
Distinguishes fra/tra (in the future), in (time taken) and fa (ago)

lesson.intro: English 'in' and 'for' split into several Italian prepositions. 'In Rome' is *a Roma* but 'in Italy' is *in Italia*. 'For three years' is *da tre anni* if it's still going on, but *per tre anni* if it's over. These are among the most frequent mistakes even at C1, because English gives no clue.

rules.title: Cities vs countries
rules.text: **A** with cities, towns and small islands (*a Roma, a Capri*). **In** with countries, regions, large islands and continents (*in Italia, in Toscana, in Sicilia, in Asia*). Plural or qualified names take the articulated preposition: *negli Stati Uniti, nei Paesi Bassi, nell'Italia del Sud*. The same preposition is used for 'in' and 'to'.

head: Place
Preposition
Example
rows: Vivo a Milano. Vado a Napoli.
Siamo stati a Capri / a Ischia.
in Francia, in Puglia, in Sardegna

rules.title: Streets, buildings, rooms
rules.text: **In** with streets and squares (*in via Manzoni, in piazza Duomo*) and many places ending in *-ia / -eria* or of work and study: *in banca, in ufficio, in biblioteca, in farmacia, in centro, in montagna, in campagna*. But **a/al** with others: *a casa, a scuola, a teatro, al cinema, al mare, al bar, all'università*. Learn them as chunks.

examples.en: I live on Via Garibaldi.
In summer we go to the seaside, in winter to the mountains.

rules.title: Da + person
rules.text: To go to or be at someone's home or workplace, use **da** + the person: *da Marco, da me, dal medico, dal parrucchiere*. Never ~~a Marco~~ or ~~al medico~~ in this sense.

examples.en: Tonight we're having dinner at Giulia's.
Tomorrow I'm going to the dentist's.

rules.title: Time: fra/tra, in, fa
rules.text: **Fra / tra** + time = 'in' (from now, future): *Torno fra un'ora*. **In** + time = time taken: *L'ho finito in due ore*. **Fa** (after the time) = ago: *tre giorni fa*.

examples.en: The train leaves in ten minutes.

examples.it: Ho scritto la tesi **in** sei mesi.
examples.en: I wrote my thesis in six months.

rules.title: Da vs per: duration
rules.text: For something that **started in the past and is still going on**, Italian uses the **present tense + da** (English uses 'have been doing… for'). For a **finished** or limited period, use **per** (often optional) with a past tense.

head: English
Italian
Why
rows: I've been studying Italian for three years.
I studied Italian for three years.

mistakes.wrong: Ho studiato l'italiano da tre anni.
mistakes.right: Ho studiato l'italiano per tre anni.

mistakes.why: To someone's place or office: *da* + person.
Plural country names take the article: *negli*.

tips: If you'd say 'have been …ing for' in English, it's almost always present + *da* in Italian.
*Fra* and *tra* are interchangeable. Pick the one that sounds better: *tra fratelli*, *fra tre giorni*.
*In via* is standard; Romans often say *a via*, but don't copy it in writing.

exercises.prompt: Mia sorella vive ___ Milano da due anni.

traps.why: Cities take *a*: *a Milano*. 'In Milan' is a classic English calque.

exercises.en: My sister has lived in Milan for two years.

exercises.prompt: Quest'estate andiamo ___ Spagna.

traps.why: Singular countries usually take plain *in*, without the article.

exercises.en: This summer we're going to Spain.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct preposition. (You still live in Italy.)
exercises.prompt: Vivo in Italia ___ cinque anni.

traps.why: Still going on → present tense + *da*. *Per* would mean a finished period.

exercises.en: I've been living in Italy for five years.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct preposition (with article if needed).
exercises.prompt: Domani devo andare ___ dentista.

traps.why: Going to a professional's: *da* + person → *dal dentista*.

exercises.explanation: To someone's place or office → **da** + article: *dal dentista*.
exercises.en: Tomorrow I have to go to the dentist's.

exercises.prompt: Aspettami, arrivo ___ dieci minuti.

optionWhy.2: *Da dieci minuti* = for the last ten minutes (ongoing).
optionWhy.3: *Dopo dieci minuti* = ten minutes later (after some other event).

exercises.en: Wait for me, I'll be there in ten minutes.

exercises.prompt: Abitiamo ___ via Manzoni, al numero 12.

traps.why: Standard Italian uses *in via* (*a via* is Roman regional usage).
No article before *via* + name: *in via Manzoni*.

exercises.explanation: Streets and squares → **in**: *in via, in piazza*.
exercises.en: We live on Via Manzoni, at number 12.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct preposition (with article if needed).
exercises.prompt: Mio fratello lavora ___ Stati Uniti.

traps.why: Plural country names take the article: *in + gli* → *negli*.
Countries take *in*, here with the article: *negli*.
*Stati* starts with *s* + consonant: the article is *gli*, so *negli*.

exercises.en: My brother works in the United States.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct preposition. (It's over now.)
exercises.prompt: Da giovane ho vissuto a Londra ___ due anni.

traps.why: The period is finished (*ho vissuto*, *da giovane*), so use *per*. *Da* is for actions still going on.
*Due anni fa* = two years ago, a point in time. Here it's a duration: *per*.

exercises.en: When I was young I lived in London for two years.

exercises.prompt: Stasera ceniamo ___ Giulia: ha cucinato le lasagne.

optionWhy.1: *A Giulia* = to Giulia (indirect object). At her place: *da Giulia*.
optionWhy.3: No article before a first name, and the preposition is *da*.

exercises.en: Tonight we're having dinner at Giulia's: she's made lasagne.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite as one sentence using the present tense and 'da'.
exercises.prompt: Ho cominciato a suonare il piano dieci anni fa e suono ancora.
answers: Suono il piano da dieci anni
Suono il pianoforte da dieci anni

traps.why: Italian uses the present for ongoing actions: *suono … da dieci anni*.

exercises.explanation: Ongoing action → present + **da**: *Suono il piano da dieci anni*.
exercises.en: I've been playing the piano for ten years.

exercises.prompt: We're going to Sardinia, to Cagliari.

traps.why: Sardinia is a large island/region: *in Sardegna*.

exercises.en: We're going to Sardinia, to Cagliari.

exercises.prompt: I've been waiting for you for an hour!

traps.why: Still waiting → present + *da*: *Ti aspetto da un'ora*.
You're still waiting, so Italian uses the present: *ti aspetto da un'ora*.

exercises.en: I've been waiting for you for an hour!

exercises.prompt: I'll be home in an hour.
exercises.explanation: *A casa* (no article) and **fra** + time = in (from now).

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct preposition. (Meaning: it took me three hours.)
exercises.prompt: Ho finito tutto il lavoro ___ tre ore: un record!

traps.why: *Fra tre ore* = three hours from now. Time taken is *in*.
*Per tre ore* = for three hours (activity), not 'within'. Time taken to complete: *in*.
*Da* is for ongoing durations. Time taken: *in*.

exercises.en: I finished all the work in three hours: a record!

exercises.prompt: Tell a new colleague that you've been living in Bologna for two years (and still do).
answers: Sono a Bologna da due anni

traps.why: Still true → present tense: *vivo a Bologna da due anni*.

exercises.en: I've been living in Bologna for two years.

exercises.prompt: Sono nato ___ Napoli, ma sono cresciuto ___ Calabria.

optionWhy.3: Both are the wrong way round: city → *a*, region → *in*.

exercises.en: I was born in Naples, but I grew up in Calabria.

exercises.prompt: D'estate andiamo al mare, d'inverno ___ montagna.

traps.why: Fixed chunk: *in montagna* (but *al mare*). Learn them as pairs.

exercises.en: In summer we go to the seaside, in winter to the mountains.

concepts.title: Prepositional phrases and adjective/noun + preposition
concepts.rule: Learn prepositional phrases and adjectives as chunks with their preposition: in base a, a causa di, grazie a, nei confronti di, a prescindere da, in vista di, a favore di, per quanto riguarda; capace di, pronto a, interessato a, contento di, diverso da, dipendere da.
assessment: Uses complex prepositions (in base a, a causa di, nei confronti di, a prescindere da, in vista di, a favore di) with the right preposition
Uses adjectives with their preposition (capace di, pronto a, interessato a, contento di, diverso da)
Avoids calques from English (dipende di, interessato in, diverso di)
Chooses between near-synonyms (a causa di / grazie a; nei confronti di / rispetto a)

lesson.intro: At C1 your Italian gets judged on precision: *a prescindere da*, *nei confronti di*, *in vista di* give formal writing its texture. These phrases are where English calques hide: 'depend **on**' becomes ~~dipende di~~, 'interested **in**' becomes ~~interessato in~~. Learn each one with its preposition as a single chunk.

rules.title: Cause, basis, result
rules.text: *A causa di* (because of, usually negative), *grazie a* (thanks to, positive), *in base a* (on the basis of, according to), *in seguito a* (following), *per via di* (informal 'because of'). The final preposition combines with the article: *a causa **del** maltempo*.

examples.it: Il volo è stato cancellato **a causa del** maltempo.
examples.en: The flight was cancelled because of bad weather.

examples.it: **Grazie al** tuo aiuto ce l'abbiamo fatta.
examples.en: Thanks to your help we made it.

examples.it: Il prezzo varia **in base alla** stagione.
examples.en: The price varies according to the season.

rules.title: Attitude, relation, position
rules.text: *Nei confronti di* (towards, with regard to), *a favore di* / *contro* (for / against), *rispetto a* (compared with), *per quanto riguarda* / *riguardo a* (as regards), *a prescindere da* (regardless of).

examples.it: È sempre gentile **nei confronti dei** clienti.
examples.en: He's always polite towards customers.
I'm in favour of the proposal.

examples.it: **A prescindere dal** risultato, sono fiero di te.
examples.en: Regardless of the result, I'm proud of you.

rules.title: Time and purpose
rules.text: *In vista di* (in view of, ahead of), *al fine di* + infinitive (in order to, formal), *a partire da* (starting from), *entro* (by, within).

examples.it: **In vista dell'**esame, studio tutti i giorni.
examples.en: With the exam coming up, I'm studying every day.

examples.it: **A partire da** lunedì, l'ufficio apre alle otto.
examples.en: Starting Monday, the office opens at eight.

rules.title: Adjective + preposition
rules.text: Many adjectives have a fixed preposition, often different from English.

rules.title: Verbs and nouns with tricky prepositions

examples.en: It depends on you.
She has a strong interest in art.

mistakes.wrong: Non è capace a dire di no.
mistakes.right: Non è capace di dire di no.

tips: *A causa di* is for negative causes; for positive ones use *grazie a*. *A causa dell'aiuto* sounds odd.
*Nei confronti di* is a neutral-formal 'towards'. In speech *con* often does the job: *È gentile con tutti*.
Write chunks, not words, in your vocabulary notes: *a prescindere da*, not just *prescindere*.

exercises.prompt: Sono molto interessato ___ questo corso.
exercises.en: I'm very interested in this course.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct preposition (with article if needed).
exercises.prompt: Il volo è stato cancellato a causa ___ maltempo.

traps.why: The phrase is *a causa di*: *a causa del maltempo*.

exercises.en: The flight was cancelled because of bad weather.

exercises.prompt: Sei pronto ___ partire? Il taxi è arrivato.
exercises.en: Are you ready to leave? The taxi's here.

exercises.prompt: Il problema è che non è capace ___ dire di no.
exercises.en: The problem is he can't say no.

exercises.prompt: Vengo o non vengo? Dipende ___ te.
exercises.en: Shall I come or not? It's up to you.

exercises.prompt: Il prezzo delle camere varia ___ alla stagione.

optionWhy.1: *A causa* is followed by *di*, and means 'because of'.
optionWhy.2: *Nei confronti* is followed by *di* and means 'towards'.
optionWhy.3: *A prescindere* is followed by *da* and means 'regardless of'.

exercises.explanation: *In base a* = according to, on the basis of: **in base alla** stagione.
exercises.en: The price of the rooms varies according to the season.

exercises.instruction: Complete with a two-word phrase meaning 'towards / with regard to'.
exercises.prompt: Il suo comportamento ___ dei colleghi è stato scorretto.

traps.why: *In confronto a* = compared with. 'Towards' is *nei confronti di*.
The fixed phrase is plural: *nei confronti di*.

exercises.explanation: **Nei confronti di** = towards, with regard to.
exercises.en: His behaviour towards his colleagues was improper.

exercises.prompt: Ti voglio bene ___ da quello che dici.

traps.why: *Nonostante* doesn't take *da*. With *da* the phrase is *a prescindere da*.

exercises.en: I love you regardless of what you say.

exercises.prompt: Sono davvero contento ___ vederti!

optionWhy.2: *Contento per* + noun = happy for someone (*Sono contento per te*). With an infinitive: *di*.

exercises.en: I'm really glad to see you!

exercises.prompt: Molti cittadini sostengono la nuova legge.
answers: Molti cittadini sono a favore della nuova legge

traps.match: Molti cittadini sono a favore di la nuova legge
Molti cittadini sono in favore della nuova legge
traps.why: *In favore di* also exists, but *a favore di* is the more common form.

traps.match: Molti cittadini sono a favore per la nuova legge

exercises.en: Many citizens are in favour of the new law.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian, using 'in vista di'.
exercises.prompt: With the exam coming up, I'm studying every day.
answers: In vista dell'esame[,] (studio|sto studiando) (tutti i giorni|ogni giorno)

traps.why: The phrase is *in vista di*: *in vista dell'esame*.

exercises.explanation: **In vista dell'**esame = ahead of / with a view to the exam.
exercises.en: With the exam coming up, I'm studying every day.

exercises.prompt: This model is different from the previous one.
answers: Questo modello è (diverso|differente) (da quello precedente|dal precedente|da quello di prima)
exercises.en: This model is different from the previous one.

exercises.prompt: We're satisfied with the results.

exercises.instruction: Say it aloud in a meeting (or type).
exercises.prompt: Say: 'Regardless of the cost, we must finish the project.'
answers: A prescindere (dal costo|dai costi)[,] dobbiamo (finire|completare|terminare) il progetto
exercises.explanation: **A prescindere da** + article: *dal costo / dai costi*.
exercises.en: Regardless of the cost, we must finish the project.

exercises.prompt: Sono stanco ___ sentire sempre le stesse scuse.

traps.why: *Stanco da* (+ noun) can mean 'tired from', but 'tired of doing' is *stanco di*.

exercises.en: I'm tired of hearing the same excuses all the time.

exercises.prompt: ___ quanto riguarda il budget, ne parliamo domani.

optionWhy.1: The fixed phrase is *per quanto riguarda*.
optionWhy.2: The fixed phrase is *per quanto riguarda*.
optionWhy.3: Calque of 'on'. The phrase is *per quanto riguarda*.

exercises.explanation: **Per quanto riguarda** = as regards, as for.
exercises.en: As for the budget, we'll talk about it tomorrow.

exercises.prompt: Thanks to your help, we made it.
answers: Grazie al tuo aiuto[,] (ce l'abbiamo fatta|ci siamo riusciti|ci siamo riuscite)

traps.why: *A causa di* is for negative causes. For a positive one: *grazie a*.

exercises.en: Thanks to your help, we made it.
